In 1966, British soccer legend Geoff Hurst scored a controversial goal against Germany in the World Cup final. His right-footed shot struck the crossbar and bounced near the goal line before spinning away, leaving confusion about whether it had fully crossed the line. Despite the uncertainty, officials awarded the goal, helping England secure its first and only World Cup title—a result still debated by German fans. "They can't take it away now anyway," Hurst told The Telegraph last year. "It is in the book." 

To avoid similar controversies over "ghost goals," soccer’s governing bodies have turned to technology, with help from a German company. For the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, FIFA is paying nearly $3.5 million to GoalControl, a German startup, to operate new goal-line technology. GoalControl installs 14 cameras in each of the 12 stadiums, taking up to 500 images per second to track the ball with precision. Combined with sensors on the goal line, this system can instantly alert referees on their smartwatches when a goal is scored, eliminating the need for lengthy consultations or replays.

The idea came from GoalControl founder Dirk Broichhausen, who, after seeing a disputed goal in Germany, began working with technicians to develop a solution.

For years, FIFA President Sepp Blatter was hesitant to introduce technology, voicing concerns about increased stoppages and limiting officials’ authority. His stance changed after a notorious "ghost goal" in the 2010 World Cup: England's Frank Lampard scored against Germany, but the goal was not given, though replays later showed it had clearly crossed the line. Germany went on to win 4-1, but the incident led Blatter to support goal-line technology.

Debate continues over using technology in soccer. UEFA President Michel Platini, who runs competitions such as the Champions League, remains against it, preferring extra referees and noting that the estimated €52 million (about $70 million) implementation cost would be better spent on youth and infrastructure. Cost is also a barrier for Major League Soccer (MLS), which supports the idea but has yet to adopt goal-line technology due to financial and logistical concerns.

Other professional sports, such as Major League Baseball, have already expanded the use of instant replay. Geoff Hurst, meanwhile, welcomes the development: "If we had this system 50 years ago, it would have shown quite clearly the ball was at least a foot over the line," he said.

V kombinaci se senzory na brankové čáře dokáže systém okamžitě upozornit rozhodčího na jeho chytrých hodinkách, že padl gól, a odpadá tak nutnost dlouhých konzultací nebo opakovaných záběrů.

S myšlenkou přišel zakladatel GoalControlu Dirk Broichhausen poté, co viděl sporný gól během zápasu v Německu a začal okamžitě hledat technické řešení.

Prezident FIFA Sepp Blatter dlouho zavádění technologií odmítal z obav o prodlužování hry a omezení rozhodčího vlivu. Změnil však názor po známém „duchovním gólu“ na mistrovství světa 2010: Angličan Frank Lampard proti Německu skóroval, ale gól uznán nebyl, přestože opakované záběry jasně ukázaly, že míč přešel čáru. Německo zápas vyhrálo 4:1, ale incident přiměl Blattera zavedení nové technologie podpořit.

Debata kolem technologií pokračuje. Náklady jsou překážkou i pro americkou MLS, která myšlenku podporuje, ale dosud ji kvůli financím a logistice nezavedla.

Jiné profesionální sporty, jako je baseball, už používají rozšířené opakované záběry při rozhodování. Geoff Hurst nový vývoj vítá: „Kdybychom měli tento systém před 50 lety, jasně by ukázal, že míč byl minimálně o stopu za čárou,“ řekl.

article_content: Haitian police have taken Joseph Felix Badio, a former official from the justice ministry, into custody for allegedly masterminding the assassination of President Jovenel Moise. Badio was detained while driving out of a supermarket parking lot in Port-au-Prince. The president was killed in his bedroom by Colombian mercenaries in 2021—a crime that triggered enduring political chaos and a sharp increase in violence in Haiti. Most of those involved in the attack have since been apprehended or killed. Badio is accused of ordering the hitmen and faces charges including murder, attempted murder, and armed robbery. He had been dismissed from his anti-corruption post a few months before the assassination after reportedly accepting a bribe to release a prisoner. Some of those arrested soon after the killing claim Badio, now 60, directed their actions. Other key suspects, including former Haitian senator John Joel Joseph and Haitian-Chilean businessman Rodolphe Jaar, have been convicted in the United States. U.S. authorities have additionally charged Venezuelan-American Antonio Intriago, the owner of CTU Security in Florida, with recruiting the mercenaries; he faces conspiracy charges. Since the president's death, Haiti’s government has struggled to maintain basic public services. Armed gangs now control much of Port-au-Prince, running aspects of city life but also intimidating residents and waging violent turf wars. The situation has forced thousands to flee their homes, and thousands have died in 2024 alone. The United Nations has recently authorized an international police mission for Haiti, with Kenya taking the lead. Despite the approval, only a few countries have pledged personnel, and the mission has not yet begun.

A British soldier, Sergeant Lee Davidson, was killed by a Taliban bomb after US troops failed to detect an 80kg improvised explosive device (IED) buried in a road in Afghanistan. Davidson’s unit was allowed to travel along a 'high-risk' route in Helmand after US forces had declared it clear of IEDs just an hour before, using vehicles equipped with advanced electronic detection equipment. However, the US Army squad did not leave their vehicles to perform visual checks for signs of tampering or hidden devices.

Shortly after, Davidson’s armored Ridgback vehicle struck the undetected IED, causing the vehicle to flip and resulting in fatal injuries. At the time, his wife, Samantha Davidson, was seven months pregnant with their third child. 

During the inquest, British coroner Nicola Mundy and experts criticized the American engineers for providing inadequate advice to UK commanders and failing to recommend more thorough checks on foot. Lieutenant Colonel Carl Frankland, a British Army IED expert, testified that the US team should have dismounted for closer inspection, which might have uncovered the bomb’s command wire. He noted that while dismounted searches are time-consuming, they are crucial on risky routes. 

Major Chris Sargeant, Davidson’s commanding officer, stated that he chose the route based on US intelligence and would have considered a different approach in hindsight. Following Davidson’s death, new guidance on route assessments and IED searches was issued to British forces. 

Samantha Davidson, left with three young children, expressed pride in her late husband, who was assisting in training Afghan police. Sergeant Davidson was the 427th member of UK forces to die in Afghanistan since operations began in 2001. His funeral was held at St Nicholas Church in Thorne, South Yorkshire, the same church where he and Samantha married in 2011.

article_content: The Mail on Sunday won one of the newspaper industry’s top honours last week, being named Sunday Newspaper of the Year at the London Press Club awards. Judges praised the paper for delivering 'more scoops, more must-read columnists, and a series of riveting exposés.' The Mail on Sunday beat out a shortlist including the Sunday Times and Sunday Telegraph. The award-winning coverage included a series of exclusive reports on the Leveson Inquiry by Political Editor Simon Walters. Prominent columnists such as Liz Jones, Rachel Johnson, Peter Hitchens, Piers Morgan, James Forsyth, Patrick Collins, Gary Neville, and Chris Evans were highlighted as 'must-read.' The award was presented at a lunch at the City of London’s Stationers’ Hall in recognition of the newspaper’s 2012 performance, its first year under fifth editor Geordie Greig. The judges described Greig’s approach as a 'radical if subtle blueprint for the paper.' Throughout the year, the Mail on Sunday reported and campaigned against widespread closures of hospital accident and emergency departments. The paper also serialised books by Salman Rushdie, Rod Stewart, Delia Smith, and Pippa Middleton. You magazine featured celebrity interviews and photoshoots with stars like One Direction, the Kardashian sisters, Charlize Theron, Leona Lewis, and Myleene Klass. The judges also commended the newspaper’s commercial achievements, with circulation reaching 1.7 million while market share and profits increased. The story continues this year with the launch of Event, the paper’s new culture, celebrity, and critics magazine—a testament to the ongoing quality and success of the Mail on Sunday.

article_content: Melting ice at the poles could lead to sea levels rising by up to three feet (around one meter) by the end of this century, according to scientists. There is a 1 in 20 chance that ocean levels around the British coast could be about a meter higher by 2100 due to climate change. Such a rise would challenge London’s existing sea defenses, putting the city at risk of flooding as often as once a decade. Researchers from the European Ice2sea programme—including experts from the British Antarctic Survey and the University of Bristol—used climate models to predict how polar ice melt will affect future sea levels. Their report is among the most detailed analyses to date of ice loss from Greenland, Antarctica, and glaciers worldwide. In a ‘medium’ climate change scenario, scientists estimate that melting ice could add between 3.5cm (1.4 inches) and 36.8cm (14 inches) to average global sea levels by 2100. Added to this, warmer temperatures cause seas to expand, potentially doubling the increase from melting ice. When accounting for these factors, as well as storm surges and changing weather patterns, overall global sea level rise by 2100 is projected to range from 6cm (2.4 inches) to 69cm (27 inches). The higher end of these estimates would have especially severe effects on low-lying island nations such as Tuvalu and the Maldives, and pose increased risks to major cities like London and New York, which would need upgraded flood defenses. London’s Thames Barrier, for example, could be less effective against frequent and severe storm surges, with protection dropping from once in a thousand years to once every twelve years if seas rise by a meter. Professor David Vaughan of the British Antarctic Survey, who coordinates the research, explained: “As glaciers and ice sheets lose ice, the resulting meltwater flows into rivers and seas, raising global sea levels. Current rates of sea level rise are already affecting vulnerable communities and ecosystems, and some future ice loss and sea level rise is likely unavoidable. Understanding what is happening now and how changes could accelerate in the future is essential for the security of our coastlines.” The study adds that sea level rise will not stop with 2100; increases between 2100 and 2200 are expected to be even greater if climate change accelerates. Such rises could devastate island states like the Maldives and heavily impact large cities. For instance, flooding like that caused by Superstorm Sandy could hit New York City every two years if sea levels rise by five feet by 2100. There is ongoing debate about constructing a $17 billion flood barrier system in New York, along with $12 billion for additional protections.

article_content: Storm surges and flooding along Canada's coasts have shifted from rare disasters to expected seasonal events. What were once considered freak natural occurrences are now becoming regular and predictable. The typical response has been to build hard walls and barriers to protect property and infrastructure, but these methods are proving increasingly ineffective and unaffordable. It's time to move beyond the status quo and consider nature-based solutions to protect our coastlines. Throughout history, people worldwide have felt a deep connection to coastal areas, building communities, sharing stories, and relying on the land that meets the sea. Indigenous Peoples, in particular, have long inhabited the coasts, developing expertise in coastal ecosystems and using salt marshes for food and transportation. Following European settlement, many of these marshes were drained and dykes constructed for agriculture, leading to further hardening of shorelines with structures like revetments and breakwaters to protect expanding cities and transportation routes. Today, Canada's coasts are lined with extensive hard infrastructure such as seawalls, dykes, and breakwaters. Notable examples include the Canso Causeway in Nova Scotia and the Vancouver seawall. While some hard infrastructure remains essential—particularly for transportation and energy—these structures often worsen erosion in neighboring areas, are costly to maintain, and degrade over time. For example, raising the dykes along the Chignecto Isthmus is estimated to cost $189 to $300 million. Such high prices make even small protection projects impractical for many communities. In light of these challenges, there is a growing opportunity to build more sustainable protective infrastructure by integrating natural elements and processes. Nature-based solutions preserve or restore natural structures and materials in the environment, acknowledging the benefits that healthy ecosystems provide for people. Options range from fully natural approaches to hybrid systems that blend traditional engineering with natural features. Examples include realigning dykes to restore natural water flow, re-establishing salt marshes, wetland and dune restoration, and living shorelines that use plants, sand, and rocks to buffer the coast. These approaches may involve setting aside land for natural processes, protecting it from development, or allowing the coastline to evolve naturally. Unlike hard infrastructure, which weakens over time, nature-based solutions often grow stronger as plants take root, biodiversity increases, and natural systems adapt. Benefits of nature-based solutions go beyond flood and erosion control; they also prevent shoreline pollution, support biodiversity, may increase property value, and enhance human well-being. Adopting nature-based solutions requires innovation and open-mindedness, especially when stone or concrete walls feel more reliable to many. Raising public awareness and providing clear information about the costs and benefits can help build confidence in these alternatives. Success also depends on collaboration and knowledge sharing among affected communities, engineers, scientists, and policymakers. Nature-based solutions work best when they are locally tailored, with input from diverse perspectives to meet varying infrastructure, ecological, and social needs. Current policies and habits—in both government agencies and among property owners—still strongly favor hard infrastructure, and bureaucratic processes often lag behind the speed of environmental hazards. Delays or gaps in legislation, like the Coastal Protection Act in Nova Scotia, and political interests can further slow the shift to nature-based approaches. Meanwhile, more Canadians are buying homes in high-risk flood zones and relying on aging infrastructure. Updating or removing roads, bridges, and rail lines creates opportunities to incorporate nature-based solutions. Looking ahead, there are many resources available for those seeking guidance on nature-based options. Partnerships like TransCoastal Adaptations in Nova Scotia, and companies such as Helping Heal Nature and CB Wetlands and Environmental Specialists, are advancing restoration, realignment, and community stewardship. National communities of practice also support the spread of natural approaches. As understanding of nature-based solutions grows, so will opportunities to use natural processes to protect our coastlines. The evidence is clear, and the tools are available: It's time to let nature play its part in coastal defense.

Je na čase překročit zavedená schémata a zvážit přírodě blízká řešení pro ochranu našich pobřeží. Lidé po celém světě si po staletí vytvořili hluboké pouto k pobřežním oblastem—budovali zde komunity, sdíleli příběhy a žili na místech, kde se země setkává s mořem. Obzvlášť původní obyvatelé žili u pobřeží po generace, vyznali se v místních ekosystémech a využívali slaniska k obživě i dopravě. Po evropském osídlení byla tato slaniska často odvodněna a místo nich stavěny hráze pro zemědělství, což vedlo k dalšímu zpevňování pobřeží například pomocí vlnolamů a dalších staveb na ochranu měst a dopravních tras. Dnes jsou kanadská pobřeží lemována rozsáhlou infrastrukturní sítí—mořské zdi, hráze nebo vlnolamy. Mezi známé příklady patří Canso Causeway v Novém Skotsku či vancouverská pobřežní promenáda. Zatímco některé pevné stavby jsou pro dopravu a energetiku nezbytné, často zhoršují erozi v okolí, jsou drahé na údržbu a časem chátrají. Například zvýšení hrází přes Chignecto Isthmus by stálo mezi 189 a 300 miliony dolarů, což znemožňuje i menší projekty mnoha komunitám. Vzhledem k těmto výzvám vzniká příležitost stavět udržitelnější ochrannou infrastrukturu začleněním přírodních procesů a prvků. Přírodě blízká řešení chrání nebo obnovují přirozené struktury a materiály v prostředí a uznávají přínosy zdravých ekosystémů pro lidi. Možnosti sahají od ryze přírodních postupů po hybridní systémy spojující inženýrství s přírodními prvky. Patří sem například přesměrování hrází pro návrat přirozeného toku vody, opětovné zakládání slanisek, obnova mokřadů a dun, nebo “živá pobřeží”, využívající rostliny, písek a kameny k ochraně břehů. Tyto přístupy často znamenají vyčlenit území pro působení přirozených procesů, chránit ho před zástavbou a nechat pobřeží vyvíjet se přirozeně. Na rozdíl od tvrdé infrastruktury, která stárne, přírodně založená řešení většinou sílí s tím, jak rostou kořeny rostlin, přibývá biodiverzity a ekosystémy se přizpůsobují. Výhody přírodě blízkých řešení přesahují ochranu před záplavami a erozí—pomáhají filtrovat znečištění, zvyšují biodiverzitu, mohou zvýšit hodnotu nemovitostí a zlepšují kvalitu života. Zavádění těchto řešení vyžaduje inovaci a otevřenost, neboť betonové stěny stále působí mnohým jako jistější volba. Zvýšení povědomí a poskytování jasných informací o nákladech a přínosech napomůže důvěře v tyto alternativy. K úspěchu je navíc třeba spolupráce a sdílení znalostí mezi místními komunitami, inženýry, vědci a politiky. Přírodě blízká řešení fungují nejlépe, když vycházejí z místních potřeb a zahrnou různé pohledy na infrastrukturu, ekologii i sociální vazby. Současné politiky a zvyklosti, ať už u státních orgánů nebo soukromých vlastníků, stále zvýhodňují tvrdou infrastrukturu, a úřední procesy často nestíhají reagovat na rychlé změny v přírodě. Mezery v legislativě, například Zákon o ochraně pobřeží v Novém Skotsku, a politické zájmy dále brzdí přechod k přírodním postupům. Zároveň se stále více Kanaďanů stěhuje do oblastí s vysokým rizikem povodní a spolehá na stárnoucí infrastrukturu. Modernizace nebo likvidace silnic, mostů a železničních tratí nabízí šanci zavést přírodě blízká řešení. S výhledem do budoucna je k dispozici mnoho zdrojů a podpory pro ty, kteří chtějí přírodě blízké možnosti prozkoumat. Partnerství, jako je TransCoastal Adaptations v Novém Skotsku, a firmy jako Helping Heal Nature či CB Wetlands and Environmental Specialists posouvají vpřed obnovu, realignaci i komunitní péči. Celostátní sdružení přispívají k šíření těchto přístupů. Jak poroste povědomí o výhodách těchto řešení, rozšíří se i možnosti zapojit přírodní procesy do ochrany pobřeží. Důkazy jsou jasné, nástroje máme k dispozici: Je čas nechat přírodu sehrát roli v obraně pobřeží.

article_content: Grammar schools in England are planning to admit a higher proportion of students from low-income families, according to new proposals revealed yesterday. The initiative aims to give greater priority in admissions to pupils eligible for free school meals (FSM) by changing existing policies. In over-subscribed schools, FSM students who pass the 11-plus entrance test could receive the same preference currently given to children in care. Additionally, selective schools intend to hold more 11-plus 'familiarisation sessions' in collaboration with primary schools and develop entrance exams that are less susceptible to coaching, with the goal of creating a fairer admissions process. Schools Minister David Laws discussed these plans with the Commons education select committee, highlighting the government's pupil premium policy, which provides extra funding to schools based on the number of pupils eligible for FSM or in care for six months or longer. He told MPs: 'We are discussing fairer access to grammar schools for young people. We are encouraging grammar schools to consider the pupil premium as a factor in their admissions policies and to make testing fairer.' Concerns have long existed that wealthier families monopolize grammar school places through private tutoring. Some grammar schools admit students purely by ranked 11-plus scores, while others use additional criteria such as proximity to the school. Schools are now being encouraged to include FSM eligibility among their admission criteria. Barry Sindall, from the Grammar School Heads Association, said some schools already use such criteria, and more are likely to do so as they consider this issue. 'We have been working with the Department for Education to find the right approach. Each school can decide for itself, but we want to support those that choose to adopt these changes,' he said. Sindall added that grammar schools do not intend to lower academic standards, and that schools may use several categories of preference, such as favoring FSM-eligible pupils within their local area. Education charity The Sutton Trust found that only 2.7 percent of grammar school entrants are eligible for free school meals, sparking debate about access. In December, Ofsted's chief inspector Sir Michael Wilshaw argued that grammar schools mainly serve middle-class children and do not significantly improve social mobility, advising against their expansion. Schools Minister David Laws stated that parents who move to access better schools should not be criticized, emphasizing the need to broaden opportunities for children currently missing out. He also criticized complacency regarding underachievement among disadvantaged students.
translated_content: Britské gymnázia plánují podle nových návrhů přijmout vyšší podíl studentů z nízkopříjmových rodin. Iniciativa si klade za cíl zvýšit prioritu při přijímání žáků, kteří mají nárok na bezplatné školní obědy (FSM), a to změnou stávajících pravidel. V přeplněných školách by žáci s FSM, kteří úspěšně složí přijímací zkoušky 11-plus, mohli získat stejnou přednost, jaká je v současnosti poskytována dětem v péči. Selektivní školy navíc plánují pořádat více úvodních setkání k testu 11-plus ve spolupráci se základními školami a vyvíjet přijímací zkoušky, které budou méně náchylné k přípravě s pomocí lektorů, s cílem vytvořit spravedlivější přijímací proces. Ministr školství David Laws o těchto plánech diskutoval s výborem pro vzdělávání Dolní sněmovny a zdůraznil vládní politiku „pupil premium“, která poskytuje školám dodatečné finance na základě počtu žáků s nárokem na FSM nebo v péči déle než šest měsíců. Poslancům řekl: „Diskutujeme o spravedlivějším přístupu mladých lidí na gymnázia. Povzbuzujeme gymnázia, aby při tvorbě svých přijímacích pravidel zohlednila pupil premium a zajistila spravedlivější testování.“ Obavy, že místa na gymnáziích si dlouhodobě monopolizují bohatší rodiny díky soukromým doučováním, přetrvávají. Některá gymnázia přijímají žáky pouze podle pořadí výsledků 11-plus, jiná používají další kritéria, například vzdálenost bydliště od školy. Školy jsou nyní vybízeny, aby do přijímacích kritérií zahrnuly také nárok na FSM. Barry Sindall ze Sdružení ředitelů gymnázií uvedl, že některé školy už tato kritéria používají a další je pravděpodobně zváží. „Spolupracujeme s ministerstvem školství na nalezení správného přístupu. Každá škola se rozhoduje sama, ale chceme podpořit ty, které se pro tuto změnu rozhodnou,“ řekl. Sindall dodal, že gymnázia nemají v úmyslu snižovat akademickou úroveň a že školy mohou využívat několik kategorií přednosti, například zvýhodnění žáků s FSM ve svém regionu. Vzdělávací charita The Sutton Trust zjistila, že pouze 2,7 % žáků přijatých na gymnázia má nárok na bezplatné školní obědy, což vyvolalo debatu o přístupu. V prosinci hlavní školní inspektor Sir Michael Wilshaw uvedl, že gymnázia především slouží dětem ze střední třídy a významně nezlepšují sociální mobilitu a doporučil, aby se jejich počet nerozšiřoval. Ministr školství David Laws rovněž uvedl, že rodiče, kteří se stěhují kvůli lepším školám, by neměli být kritizováni, a zdůraznil potřebu rozšířit příležitosti pro děti, které je zatím nemají. Kritizoval také toleranci k neúspěchu u znevýhodněných žáků.

article_content: South Africans of all backgrounds spent a second night together, singing, dancing, and mourning as they celebrated the life of Nelson Mandela, the man who helped bridge the nation's racial divide. As the country continued to process Mandela's death at age 95, hundreds gathered outside his former home in Soweto, where he lived as a young lawyer. At Mandela's residence in the Houghton area of Johannesburg, where he spent his final months, more people of all backgrounds came to pay tribute. A large number of floral tributes have been placed outside Mandela's Houghton home. Crowds gathered again in Soweto, another place deeply connected to Mandela's life. Ariel Sobel, a white man born in 1993—one year before Mandela became president—said, 'What I liked most about Mandela was his forgiveness, his passion, his diversity, the impact of what he did.' As twelve doves were released, people sang traditional songs, the national anthem, 'Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika' (God Bless Africa, the anthem of the anti-apartheid struggle), and Christian hymns. Many wore traditional clothing from the nation's Zulu, Xhosa, and other ethnic groups. A mourner held up a poster reading, 'He will rule the universe with God.' President Jacob Zuma announced a series of ceremonies expected to draw large numbers of dignitaries from around the world as well as local mourners. Mourners signed a condolence book in Johannesburg, while others watched a film about Mandela's life on a big screen. Throughout the night, South Africans lit candles in Houghton as they remembered their leader with posters and flags bearing Mandela's image. At least three American presidents will travel to South Africa to attend the memorial services. The White House said that President Barack Obama and First Lady Michelle Obama would go to South Africa to pay their respects, accompanied by former President George W. Bush and Laura Bush. Travel details were still being arranged, but it was not clear when they would depart. President Obama confirmed he would attend the funeral with his wife Michelle. Former President Bill Clinton also said he and his family plan to go to South Africa, along with his wife, former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton; it was uncertain whether they would fly on Air Force One. Clinton told CNN, 'My whole family will be there, and we're looking forward to having the chance to say good-bye one last time.' Residents in Soweto read news about Mandela's passing, and South Africans of all ages continued to hold gatherings and services in his memory. Many mourners attended special church services, including in Soweto, where Mandela once lived as a child. A man was seen lighting a candle outside Mandela's former home, now a museum, in Soweto. Obama also invited 89-year-old former President George H. W. Bush, but his spokesman said he could not travel. Mandela's death has led to an outpouring of memorials and celebrations of the former political prisoner who became president and was key to ending apartheid. After Mandela's death, Obama remarked that he was one of the millions inspired by Mandela's example. Obama said Thursday, 'Like so many around the globe, I cannot fully imagine my own life without the example that Nelson Mandela set.' Two women comforted each other on Vilakazi Street in Soweto, where Mandela once lived, and a mother consoled her son as people continued to gather to mourn. For Obama and Bush, the trip to South Africa will be the second time they have been on the continent together this year. They were both in Tanzania in the summer, with their visits coinciding for a short time. The two briefly met to honor the victims of the 1998 U.S. Embassy bombing in Dar es Salaam. Their wives attended an African first ladies' summit during that trip. In New York City, the Empire State Building was lit in the colors of the South African flag as a tribute to Mandela, and an impromptu shrine was created on the street as people paid their respects.
translated_content: Jihofričané všech ras strávili druhou noc společně zpěvem, tancem a smutkem, když oslavovali život Nelsona Mandely, muže, který pomohl překlenout rasové rozdíly v zemi. Zatímco země se stále vyrovnávala se smrtí Mandely ve věku 95 let, stovky lidí se shromáždily před jeho bývalým domem v Sowetu, kde žil jako mladý právník. V Mandelově rezidenci v oblasti Houghton v Johannesburgu, kde strávil své poslední měsíce, přišlo uctít památku více lidí všech etnik. Před Mandelovým domem v Houghtonu bylo položeno velké množství květin. Davy se znovu sešly v Sowetu, dalším místě úzce spojeném s jeho životem. Ariel Sobel, běloch narozený v roce 1993 – rok předtím, než se Mandela stal prezidentem – řekl: 'Nejvíc se mi na Mandelovi líbila jeho odpuštění, vášeň, rozmanitost a dopad toho, co udělal.' Když bylo vypuštěno dvanáct holubic, lidé zpívali tradiční písně, státní hymnu, 'Nkosi Sikelel’ iAfrika' (Bože, žehnej Africe, hymnu proti apartheidu) a křesťanské chorály. Mnozí měli tradiční oděvy národa Zulu, Xhosa a dalších etnických skupin. Jeden z truchlících držel plakát s nápisem: 'Bude vládnout vesmíru s Bohem.' Prezident Jacob Zuma oznámil sérii obřadů, které mají přilákat mnoho světových státníků i domácích smutečních hostů. Lidé podepisovali kondolenční knihu v Johannesburgu, zatímco jiní sledovali na velkoplošné obrazovce film o Mandelově životě. Po celou noc Jihoafričané zapalovali svíčky v Houghtonu a připomínali si svého vůdce s plakáty a vlajkami s jeho podobiznou. Do Jižní Afriky přijedou alespoň tři američtí prezidenti na pohřební služby. Bílý dům oznámil, že prezident Barack Obama s manželkou Michelle pojedou do Jižní Afriky vzdát úctu a připojí se k nim bývalý prezident George W. Bush a Laura Bushová. Detaily cesty se stále domlouvají, zatím není jasné, kdy vyrazí. Prezident Obama potvrdil účast na pohřbu se svou manželkou Michelle. Bývalý prezident Bill Clinton také uvedl, že plánuje se svou rodinou cestovat do Jižní Afriky, spolu s manželkou, bývalou ministryní zahraničí Hillary Clintonovou; nebylo jasné, zda poletí Air Force One. Clinton řekl CNN: 'Celá moje rodina tam bude a těšíme se, že budeme mít možnost se naposledy rozloučit.' Obyvatelé Soweta si četli zprávy o Mandelově smrti a Jihofričané všech generací dál pořádají setkání a bohoslužby na jeho počest. Mnoho smutečních hostů se účastnilo speciálních bohoslužeb, například v Sowetu, kde Mandela žil jako dítě. Muž byl viděn, jak zapaluje svíčku před bývalým Mandelovým domem, nyní muzeem, v Sowetu. Obama pozval i bývalého prezidenta George H. W. Bushe, ale jeho mluvčí oznámil, že nemůže cestovat. Mandelova smrt vedla k přívalu vzpomínek a oslav někdejšího politického vězně, který se stal prezidentem a klíčovou postavou při ukončení apartheidu. Po Mandelově smrti Obama prohlásil, že patří mezi miliony lidí, které Mandela inspiroval. Obama řekl ve čtvrtek: 'Stejně jako mnozí po celém světě si neumím představit svůj život bez příkladu Nelsona Mandely.' Na ulici Vilakazi v Sowetu, kde Mandela kdysi žil, se dvě ženy navzájem utěšovaly a matka utěšovala svého syna při dalším smutečním shromáždění. Pro Obamu a Bushe bude cesta do Jižní Afriky už druhou návštěvou kontinentu letos. Oba byli v létě v Tanzanii, kde se jejich cesty na krátkou dobu setkaly. Krátce se sešli, aby uctili oběti bombového útoku na americké velvyslanectví v Dar es Salaamu v roce 1998. Jejich manželky se v té době zúčastnily summitu afrických prvních dam. V New Yorku byla Empire State Building nasvícena v barvách jihoafrické vlajky na poctu Mandelovi a na ulici vzniklo improvizované pietní místo.

Just shy of his 21st birthday, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain has kept his spirits high after a challenging season in which injuries forced him to miss both the World Cup and Arsenal’s first trophy win in nine years. Reflecting on the past year, Oxlade-Chamberlain said, “What have I learned? Don’t get injured. It’s not nice.” He remains optimistic, with the upcoming FA Community Shield against Manchester City providing a fresh start for the England midfielder.

Oxlade-Chamberlain sustained a cruciate knee ligament injury on the opening day of last season but made a strong return in January. Unfortunately, he was sidelined again by a groin issue later in the campaign. Although declared fit for the World Cup, he suffered another minor knee injury during a warm-up match against Ecuador in Miami. Despite being kept in Roy Hodgson’s England squad, a subsequent setback prevented him from playing in the tournament’s final match against Costa Rica.

Oxlade-Chamberlain spoke about learning to manage difficult periods, explaining, “It’s tough to watch your teammates win while you can’t play. But with a positive attitude, you come out stronger. During rehabilitation, you focus on areas you usually overlook, like core strength, pelvic floor, and flexibility – all important for injury prevention. I’ve learned to take better care of my body.”

He remains upbeat at Arsenal, where excitement is building after their FA Cup victory. “We always believed our efforts would pay off,” he noted. “Winning brings momentum and confidence. With new signings like Alexis Sanchez and our World Cup winners returning, it’s an exciting time.” Oxlade-Chamberlain has ambitious goals for the coming season: winning the Premier League, the FA Cup, and the Champions League. Arsenal will face Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a warning urging the public to stop using Magic Power Coffee, an instant coffee promoted as a sexual enhancer. According to the FDA, Magic Power Coffee contains hydroxythiohomosildenafil, a chemical compound similar to sildenafil—the active ingredient in the prescription drug Viagra. This substance can cause dangerously low blood pressure, particularly when combined with prescription medications such as nitrates.

Because Magic Power Coffee is marketed as an 'all natural dietary supplement,' some consumers may mistakenly assume it poses no health risks. In reality, said Deborah M. Autor, director of the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research Office of Compliance, Magic Power Coffee could cause serious harm. The agency cautioned that non-prescription sexual enhancement products claiming to rival prescription drugs can expose users to unpredictable dangers and even the risk of injury or death.

While the FDA has not yet received reports of adverse events linked to Magic Power Coffee, it advises anyone who experiences side effects from this product—or any similar supplement—to consult a doctor or nurse. Magic Power Coffee, which calls itself the 'world’s first passion coffee,' is available online and through independent distributors. The company has not yet responded to the FDA’s announcement. The product’s website advises consulting a physician before use, especially for those with conditions such as stroke, high blood pressure, heart, liver, kidney, or thyroid disease, diabetes, anemia, depression, anxiety, other psychiatric illnesses, a family history of these or other health issues, or those taking prescription, over-the-counter, or herbal medicines.

article_content: The NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) is scheduled for launch in the first quarter of 2024 after completing final tests, especially vibration tests, according to NASA officials. NASA NISAR Project Manager Phil Barela shared that ISRO is planning the launch for early next year at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, using the ISRO Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle Mark-II. The mission will last three years, starting after a 90-day satellite commissioning period, and will survey all of Earth's land and ice-covered surfaces every 12 days. Critical tests still to be completed include vibration, battery, simulation, and various performance tests of the radar and spacecraft electronics. NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory Director Dr. Laurie Leshin noted that NISAR brings new capabilities beyond previous missions and may operate even longer if it performs well. Jointly developed by NASA and ISRO, NISAR is a Low Earth Orbit observatory set to systematically map Earth, providing data on ecosystems, ice mass, sea levels, groundwater, and natural hazards like earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanoes, and landslides. The satellite includes Synthetic Aperture Radar instruments (L-band and S-band SAR) and an antenna reflector, capable of detecting surface changes as small as one centimetre. Weighing about 2,800 kg, NISAR is powered by two solar arrays generating around four kilowatts. The six-foot-tall spacecraft bus houses command and communication systems, supports the radar payload, and has enough fuel for at least five years of operations. The publication also discusses India's expected 6.7% GDP growth in Q2, possible GST policy modifications, advancements in green energy, and industry feedback on direct-to-mobile TV technology.

article_content: Chicken nuggets are made from chicken, but often include parts most consumers may not expect. Researchers in Mississippi performed an 'autopsy' on chicken nuggets from two fast food chains in Jackson, revealing that the nuggets contained much less meat than anticipated. One chicken nugget sample contained about 50% muscle tissue from the breast or thigh, while the remaining portion was made up of fat, blood vessels, and nerves. A second sample was found to have only 40% muscle, with the rest comprised of fat, cartilage, and even bone. The fast food chains involved were not named in the study. Dr. Richard D. deShazo, the study's lead author, advises eating white chicken meat instead of nuggets. He notes that while nuggets might appear white inside, appearances can be deceiving. "Some companies have chosen to use a processed mixture of chicken parts rather than lean white meat, coat it in batter, fry it, and still market it as chicken," Dr. deShazo told Reuters. "It's essentially a chicken by-product high in calories, salt, sugar, and fat—a very unhealthy option. Worse, kids enjoy them and they're specifically marketed to children," he said. Dr. deShazo says eating chicken nuggets occasionally is acceptable but is concerned about people who consume them several times a week. Ashley Peterson, of the National Chicken Council, disagrees that consumers are misled. She points out that nutritional facts for most fast-food products are accessible online, and grocery products include full ingredient lists. "Chicken nuggets tend to have a higher fat content because they are breaded and fried, but the ingredients are not a secret," Peterson noted.

Vedoucí studie Dr. Richard D. deShazo doporučuje jíst bílé kuřecí maso místo nuget. Upozorňuje, že ačkoli nugety mohou uvnitř vypadat bíle, vzhled může být klamný. article_content: A teenager who completed her A-levels despite having terminal cancer has been awarded "outstanding" results after her passing. Margaret Adcock, known as Maggie, died in June at the age of 18 before she could learn her exam scores. John Port Spencer Academy in Derbyshire announced that she achieved two A*s and an A. Ms Adcock's parents received the results last week, expressing that while they were "very proud," it was also "bittersweet." "Maggie worked so hard," her mother, Lyn Adcock, said. "Her determination and commitment inspire us all. She never ceased to amaze us. We always knew she could do it." Angharad Swift, assistant principal at Ms Adcock's school, said Maggie "continues to inspire us all." Mrs Swift added: "We remain deeply proud of Margaret Adcock, who sadly passed away in June. She has been awarded outstanding A-level results, reflecting the bright, ambitious, and courageous student she was." Ms Adcock, who was from Hilton in Derbyshire, studied English language, geography, and psychology at A-level and had planned to study geography at Durham University. She was diagnosed with alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma in May 2022. Although she underwent chemotherapy, she was told in January that the cancer had spread to her brain and she had only weeks or months to live. After learning that her cancer was terminal, her friends and teachers organized a spring ball for her with just two weeks of planning, fulfilling one of her wishes. She was also surprised with an 18th birthday party in May. The school now plans to celebrate her life in various ways. The new sixth form block will have a Maggie's Bench outside, and the school hopes to create a wildflower garden in her memory. Each year, the Margaret Adcock Award will be given to a student demonstrating determination, ambition, and resilience in geography. Follow BBC East Midlands on Facebook, X, and Instagram. article_content: An English tourist was fined £150 for making a racist comment at a Welsh holiday park. Anthony Taaffe, 47, from Bolton, Greater Manchester, was found guilty in Llandudno of racially aggravated disorderly conduct. The offense happened at Presthaven Sands holiday park near Prestatyn, when Taaffe, upset over property theft and reportedly intoxicated, insulted security staff with a derogatory term referencing Welsh people. Taaffe defended his language in court, claiming it referred to countryside residents in general. When an off-duty Welsh police officer intervened, Taaffe responded with further profanity. He repeated similar remarks while being restrained and in police custody. The judge criticized the use of such language, especially around children, as unacceptable. Taaffe’s defense highlighted his epilepsy and receipt of benefits. The article also mentions Petra Mills, fined £110 in Monmouth for a racially aggravated insult, and Darren Swain, a postman in Coventry, ordered to do community service and pay costs for anti-Scottish graffiti. These examples signal increasing legal measures against racially abusive language in the UK.

Incident se odehrál v rekreačním parku Presthaven Sands u Prestatynu, kde Taaffe – rozrušený krádeží svého majetku a údajně pod vlivem alkoholu – urazil pracovníky ostrahy hanlivým výrazem na adresu Velšanů. article_content: A survey of nearly 600 people conducted by three Penn State Abington students found little difference between men and women in Thanksgiving preparation and hosting roles. However, both men and women reported that planning for the holiday often causes family tension. Students Kyleigh Byers (senior, psychological and social sciences), Emma Jamison (junior, criminal justice), and Sophia Montany (junior, psychology) led the study, 'Cooking, Cleaning and Contributions: Exploring Gendered Division of Labor in Thanksgiving Family Celebrations.' Their faculty adviser, Beth Montemurro, a distinguished professor of sociology, also expressed surprise at the results. Montemurro suggested that the sample may be self-selecting; those who participate in planning Thanksgiving were probably more likely to respond. She also noted that respondents may have answered based on their household routines rather than their individual actions. The survey examined age and gender differences in labor for Thanksgiving—including planning, preparation, cooking, cleaning, and communication with friends and family—along with associated feelings. Despite a nearly equal reported division of labor, many participants said Thanksgiving is a source of family tension. Among respondents over 40, 32% of men and 28% of women agreed the holiday caused stress. For those under 40, 53% of men and 38% of women said Thanksgiving brought strain. Additional findings: Women over 40 felt they planned Thanksgiving better than their partners, while women under 40 said their work was more appreciated. 96% of respondents reported being involved in planning, and 61% of men and 65% of women enjoyed making arrangements for Thanksgiving. 59% of men and 47% of women spent more than 10 hours preparing. Enjoyment of cooking for Thanksgiving was similar for both genders. Participants were U.S. residents aged 25-75, in committed relationships for at least three years, and most were between 30 and 39 years old. Nearly 90% identified as white/Caucasian. The idea for the study was inspired by previous literature on women and 'kinkeeping'—the emotional and physical labor of maintaining family connections. Montemurro shared that all three students participated in her Sociology of Gender course before joining the research program. Montemurro stated they plan to gather more data and potentially publish findings after further analyses, considering factors such as income and work hours. The students presented these survey results at the Eastern Sociological Society Annual Meeting in Baltimore earlier this year.

Přesto však muži i ženy uvedli, že plánování svátku často vede k napětí v rodině. Studentky Kyleigh Byers (posluchačka posledního ročníku, psychologické a sociální vědy), Emma Jamison (třetí ročník, kriminologie) a Sophia Montany (třetí ročník, psychologie) vedly studii „Vaření, úklid a přispění: Zkoumání genderového rozdělení práce při rodinných oslavách Dne díkůvzdání“. Jejich odborná poradkyně, profesorka sociologie Beth Montemurro, byla výsledky také překvapená. Montemurro poznamenala, že výběr respondentů mohl být samovýběrový; ti, kteří se účastní plánování Dne díkůvzdání, spíše na průzkum odpověděli. Uvedla také, že odpovědi mohly odrážet spíše domácí rutinu než individuální činnosti. Průzkum se zaměřil na věkové a genderové rozdíly v práci spojené s Dnem díkůvzdání – plánování, příprava, vaření, úklid a komunikace s přáteli a rodinou – a také na pocity s těmito úkoly spojené. Přestože je rozdělení práce téměř rovnoměrné, mnoho účastníků uvedlo, že Den díkůvzdání je zdrojem rodinného napětí. Mezi dotazovanými nad 40 let souhlasilo 32 % mužů a 28 % žen s tím, že svátek způsobuje stres. U mladších 40 let to bylo 53 % mužů a 38 % žen. Další zjištění: Ženy nad 40 let se cítily být lepší v plánování Dne díkůvzdání než jejich partner, zatímco mladší ženy uvedly, že je jejich práce více oceněna. 96 % respondentů se podílelo na plánování, 61 % mužů a 65 % žen si přípravy svátku užívalo. 59 % mužů a 47 % žen strávilo přípravami více než 10 hodin. Ve vaření pro Den díkůvzdání nebyly žádné výrazné genderové rozdíly v oblibě. Účastníci byli obyvatelé USA ve věku 25–75 let ve stabilním vztahu trvajícím minimálně tři roky; většina byla ve věku 30–39 let a téměř 90 % se identifikovalo jako běloši. Nápad na tuto studii vzešel z předchozí literatury o tzv. „kinkeepingu“ – emocionální a fyzické práci na udržování rodinných kontaktů. Montemurro uvedla, že všechny tři studentky absolvovaly její kurz Sociologie genderu ještě před zapojením do výzkumného programu. Montemurro zmínila, že plánují získat více údajů a případně výsledky publikovat po dalších analýzách, které zohlední například příjmy nebo pracovní dobu. Studentky prezentovaly výsledky průzkumu na výročním setkání Eastern Sociological Society letos v Baltimore.

article_content: BlackBerry has agreed to sell itself for $4.7 billion, marking the end of its era as a leading smartphone company after years of significant financial losses. On Monday, BlackBerry announced it had signed a letter of intent with its largest shareholder, Fairfax Financial, a Canadian group. As part of the arrangement, BlackBerry shareholders will receive $9 in cash for each share they hold. Despite CEO Thorsten Heins' efforts to relaunch the company, BlackBerry reported losses of over $1 billion and has now decided to sell to Fairfax, its largest stakeholder. Research In Motion (RIM), BlackBerry's parent company, has seen its share of the smartphone market steadily decline while competitors like Apple's iOS and Android have risen in popularity. Fairfax Financial is led by Prem Watsa, a former BlackBerry board member who owns 10 percent of the company. Here is a brief timeline of key events in BlackBerry/RIM's history: - 1985: Research in Motion is founded in Ontario, Canada. - 1999: RIM launches its first handheld device using its proprietary email and data network. - 2001: BlackBerry becomes highly popular with business users; devices are used for communication during the September 11 attacks. - 2004: BlackBerry surpasses one million users. - 2007: Apple releases the iPhone, while BlackBerry celebrates reaching 10 million subscribers. - 2008: Introduction of the BlackBerry Storm, their first touch-screen device, which did not succeed in the market. - 2010: Release of the BlackBerry Torch, combining a touchscreen with a physical keyboard. - 2011: Company shares fall to between $5.25 and $6. - 2013: Launch of BlackBerry 10 fails to turn performance around; company reports a first-quarter loss and an additional billion-dollar loss. Prem Watsa stepped down from BlackBerry’s board last month when the company announced it was considering a sale. Watsa is well-known in Canada as a value investor. In a statement, he said: "We can deliver immediate value to shareholders, while we continue to execute a long-term strategy as a private company focused on delivering secure enterprise solutions to BlackBerry customers worldwide." Trading of BlackBerry shares was halted ahead of the news. The stock dropped sharply after the announcement of nearly $1 billion in losses and a plan to lay off 4,500 employees, representing 40 percent of its global workforce. BlackBerry is attempting to cut costs by 50 percent and refocus on its business customers. BlackBerry devices, introduced in 1999, were once so popular they earned the nickname 'CrackBerry.' Notable fans included President Barack Obama and Madonna, who famously kept her BlackBerry close at night. However, BlackBerry has struggled to compete since the iPhone was introduced. The 2013 launch of the BlackBerry 10, with devices like the Z10 touchscreen and Q10 keyboard model, aimed to revive the brand. However, these delays and weak sales failed to reverse BlackBerry's decline. At its peak in late 2009, BlackBerry smartphones held over 20 percent of the global market, according to analyst Mike Walkley of Canaccord Genuity. Today, their share has shrunk to just 1.5 percent.

V pondělí BlackBerry oznámil, že podepsal smlouvu o záměru se svým největším akcionářem, kanadskou společností Fairfax Financial. Součástí dohody je, že akcionáři BlackBerry obdrží za každou akcii 9 dolarů v hotovosti. Mateřská společnost Research In Motion (RIM) zaznamenala trvalý pokles svého podílu na trhu chytrých telefonů, zatímco konkurenti jako iOS od Applu a Android výrazně posílili. Fairfax Financial vede Prem Watsa, bývalý člen představenstva BlackBerry, který vlastní 10 procent společnosti. Zde je stručná časová osa klíčových událostí v historii BlackBerry/RIM: - 1985: Research in Motion založena v Ontariu, Kanada. - 1999: RIM uvádí svůj první přenosný přístroj využívající vlastní e-mailovou a datovou síť. - 2001: BlackBerry se stává velmi populárním u firemních uživatelů; zařízení byla využita ke komunikaci během útoků 11. září. - 2004: BlackBerry překročil hranici jednoho milionu uživatelů. - 2007: Apple uvádí iPhone, zatímco BlackBerry slaví dosažení 10 milionů uživatelů. - 2008: Uvedení BlackBerry Storm, prvního dotykového zařízení značky, které však na trhu neuspělo. - 2010: Uvedení BlackBerry Torch, které kombinuje dotykovou obrazovku a fyzickou klávesnici. - 2011: Akcie společnosti klesají na hodnotu 5,25 až 6 dolarů. - 2013: Uvedení BlackBerry 10 nezvrátilo špatné výsledky; společnost ohlašuje ztrátu za první čtvrtletí a další miliardovou ztrátu. Prem Watsa odstoupil z představenstva BlackBerry minulý měsíc, když společnost oznámila, že zvažuje prodej. Watsa je v Kanadě považován za uznávaného hodnotového investora. Ve svém vyjádření uvedl: „Můžeme akcionářům okamžitě zajistit hodnotu a zároveň pokračovat v naplňování dlouhodobé strategie jako soukromá firma zaměřená na bezpečná podniková řešení pro zákazníky BlackBerry po celém světě." Obchodování s akciemi BlackBerry bylo před oznámením pozastaveno. Akcie prudce klesly poté, co společnost oznámila téměř miliardovou ztrátu a plán na propuštění 4 500 zaměstnanců, což představuje 40 procent celkové pracovní síly. BlackBerry se snaží snížit náklady o 50 procent a znovu se soustředit na firemní klientelu. Zařízení BlackBerry, představená v roce 1999, byla kdysi tak populární, že si vysloužila přezdívku ‚CrackBerry‘. Mezi slavné uživatele patřil například prezident Barack Obama a Madonna, která údajně spala s telefonem BlackBerry pod polštářem. Po příchodu iPhonu však BlackBerry začal ztrácet pozici. Uvedení BlackBerry 10 v roce 2013, včetně modelů Z10 s dotykovou obrazovkou a Q10 s klávesnicí, mělo značku znovu oživit. Tyto zpožděné a špatně prodávané modely však pokles neodvrátily. Na svém vrcholu v roce 2009 držely telefony BlackBerry přes 20 procent světového trhu, uvádí analytik Mike Walkley ze společnosti Canaccord Genuity. Dnes jejich podíl činí jen 1,5 procenta.

UK Prime Minister David Cameron called an urgent meeting today to prepare for the possibility that Greece could exit the eurozone. Cameron chaired an hour-long session with senior officials from the Treasury, Foreign Office, and Bank of England to discuss potential threats to the UK economy. At the same time, Greece's new Prime Minister, Alexis Tsipras, used his inaugural parliamentary speech to firmly state that his demand for restructuring the country's debt is non-negotiable.

Attending the meeting at 10 Downing Street were top Whitehall officials, including Treasury permanent secretary Sir Nicholas Macpherson and representatives from the Department for Business and the Bank of England’s financial regulatory division. There are concerns about the risk of financial contagion to Britain if Greece defaults.

Most of Greece’s national debt is held by eurozone institutions, not by the UK, which may limit direct impact. However, Cameron’s official spokesman warned that risks of contagion and uncertainty persist, meaning comprehensive contingency plans are vital. The meeting reflects preparations made during the peak of the Greek crisis in 2012.

Foreign Office officials updated Cameron on the political situation, while the Bank of England and Treasury outlined the risks of economic instability spreading across Europe. Downing Street stated that contingency planning would continue to intensify. Cameron’s spokesman noted significant differences from the 2012 crisis, such as lower bond yields in Portugal, Ireland, and Spain.

The UK recognizes the new Greek government's and eurozone countries’ stated intentions to maintain eurozone unity. However, uncertainties in financial markets remain as tense discussions continue between Greece and eurozone member states.

Asked about the City of London’s exposure, the Prime Minister’s spokesman explained that Greek bonds are mostly held within the eurozone, primarily due to the European Central Bank’s support for Greek financial institutions. Nevertheless, given London’s status as a major global financial center, ongoing vigilance is required.

Chancellor George Osborne recently warned that the unresolved dispute over Greek debt was becoming a major risk to the world economy, after meeting Greece’s new finance minister, Yanis Varoufakis, in London. Athens must secure about £5 billion in financing by the end of the month to sustain its economy. Failure could lead to Greece defaulting on its debts and leaving the eurozone.

Both Greece and other eurozone countries have expressed a desire to avoid a Greek exit. However, the ruling Syriza party's pledge to end austerity has created tension with other eurozone governments. Tsipras has promised to seek debt relief and to renegotiate the terms of Greece’s £185 billion bailout—a move Germany has called 'too generous.'

Osborne emphasized: 'This stand-off between Greece and the eurozone is increasing the risks every day to the British economy. A Greek exit would cause real disruptions. An international effort is needed to resolve the impasse.'

Cameron and Tsipras are scheduled to meet for the first time at an EU summit in Brussels later this week. After Syriza’s election victory, Cameron warned that it could heighten economic uncertainty across Europe.

Britský premiér David Cameron dnes svolal naléhavou schůzku, aby se připravil na možnost, že by Řecko mohlo opustit eurozónu. Setkání v Downing Street se zúčastnili hlavní úředníci státní správy, včetně stálého tajemníka ministerstva financí Sira Nicholase Macphersona a zástupců ministerstva obchodu a finančně-regulačního odboru Bank of England. Objevily se obavy z rizika finanční nákazy pro Británii v případě, že by Řecko zbankrotovalo.

Většina řeckého národního dluhu je držena institucemi eurozóny, nikoli Spojeným královstvím, což může omezit přímý dopad. Cameronův oficiální mluvčí však varoval, že rizika nákazy a nejistoty přetrvávají, a proto je nezbytné mít komplexní krizové plány. Schůzka odráží přípravy z doby největší řecké krize v roce 2012.

Zástupci zahraničí informovali Camerona o politické situaci, zatímco Bank of England a ministerstvo financí nastínili riziko rozšíření ekonomické nestability po Evropě. Podle Downing Street budou krizové přípravy dále zesilovat. Cameronův mluvčí poukázal na významné rozdíly oproti roku 2012, například na nižší výnosy dluhopisů v Portugalsku, Irsku a Španělsku.

Británie uznává deklarované záměry nové řecké vlády i zemí eurozóny zachovat jednotu eurozóny. Na finančních trzích však stále panuje nejistota kvůli napjatým diskusím mezi Řeckem a státy eurozóny.

Na dotaz ohledně expozice londýnského City mluvčí premiéra vysvětlil, že řecké dluhopisy jsou převážně drženy v eurozóně, zejména díky podpoře Evropské centrální banky řeckému finančnímu sektoru. Přesto je s ohledem na status Londýna jako významného světového finančního centra nutná zvýšená ostražitost.

Ministr financí George Osborne nedávno varoval, že nevyřešený spor ohledně řeckého dluhu se stává zásadním rizikem pro světovou ekonomiku, a to po schůzce s novým řeckým ministrem financí Yanisem Varoufakisem v Londýně. Atény musí do konce měsíce zajistit financování ve výši přibližně 5 miliard liber, aby udržely ekonomiku v chodu. Pokud se to nepodaří, hrozí Řecku platební neschopnost a odchod z eurozóny.

Řecko i ostatní státy eurozóny daly najevo, že si nepřejí, aby Řecko opustilo společnou měnu. Nicméně příslib vládní strany Syriza ukončit úsporná opatření vyostřil vztahy s ostatními vládami eurozóny. Tsipras slíbil usilovat o odpuštění části dluhu a nové vyjednání podmínek záchranného balíčku ve výši 185 miliard liber, což Německo označilo za 'příliš velkorysé.'

Osborne zdůraznil: 'Tato patová situace mezi Řeckem a eurozónou zvyšuje každý den rizika pro britskou ekonomiku. Odchod Řecka by způsobil skutečné otřesy. Je potřeba mezinárodní snahy k vyřešení slepé uličky.'

Cameron a Tsipras se mají poprvé setkat při summitu EU v Bruselu tento týden. Po vítězství Syrizy ve volbách Cameron varoval, že by to mohlo zvýšit ekonomickou nejistotu v Evropě.

article_content: A market trader has been banned from selling an anti-Taliban T-shirt by local council authorities, who were concerned it might offend some people. The T-shirt, which displays the words 'Taliban Hunting Club' around a target with a skull and two guns, has been popular among frontline soldiers and their families. Mark Brown, who operates a military goods stall at Louth market in Lincolnshire, was told by East Lindsey District Council to stop selling the shirts after a complaint from a member of the public described them as 'politically sensitive and offensive.' Brown removed the shirts immediately and started a discussion on Facebook to gauge public opinion about whether the shirts are distasteful. He explained that the T-shirt serves as a morale booster for troops and their supporters, and suggested that the council’s decision shows insensitivity towards servicemen and women. Brown has sold the shirts at various markets and events, including the Sandringham Game Fair, without previous objections. Some local traders, like Alan Grant, support Brown and argue the ban is unnecessary, while others, such as Andy Nisbet, believe the shirts could harm the market’s reputation and might be interpreted as racist. A council spokesperson said they received complaints from local residents and acted accordingly, with Brown voluntarily agreeing to withdraw the product. The incident coincides with the tenth anniversary of the start of the war in Afghanistan.

Tričko s nápisem 'Taliban Hunting Club' kolem terče se lebkou a dvěma zbraněmi je oblíbené mezi vojáky v první linii i jejich rodinami. article_content: A rare spider orchid has been found growing on the glass roof of the Swanage Sewage Treatment Works in Dorset. The plant is so rare that it is protected under Schedule 8 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act, making it illegal to uproot, cut, sell, or destroy. Staff at the sewage works noticed the orchid after hearing reports of another rare flower at the location last year, prompting them to keep an eye out for unusual plants. Ellen McDouall, a senior conservation ecologist at Wessex Water, explained, 'This roof has only existed for ten years and orchids can take that long to flower. We don't know how they arrived—whether a seed was in the soil or carried by the wind. Thankfully, the roof isn't under much operational pressure, so we hope to manage the land for the benefit of the plant.' The coastal limestone cliffs near Swanage are one of only three UK strongholds for the spider orchid, with the others located in Kent and Suffolk. A Dorset Wildlife Trust spokesman commented, 'This is a wonderful find, as the spider orchid is extremely rare in the UK.' Dorset and the Wessex Water region are rich in biodiversity, and many species and habitats in the area are legally protected. Ellen added, 'It's crucial that we regularly assess the impact of our operations on wildlife. This is central to our ongoing biodiversity action plan.'

Zaměstnanci čistírny si orchideje všimli poté, co slyšeli o nálezu jiné vzácné květiny na stejném místě minulý rok, což je přimělo dávat větší pozor na neobvyklé rostliny. Ellen McDouall, hlavní ekolog pro ochranu přírody ve společnosti Wessex Water, vysvětlila: 'Tato střecha existuje teprve deset let a orchidejím může trvat právě tolik, než vykvetou. Nevíme, jak se sem dostaly – jestli bylo semeno v půdě, nebo je přivál vítr. Naštěstí střecha není zatížena provozem, takže doufáme, že půdu pro tuto rostlinu zvládneme cíleně spravovat.' Pobřežní vápencové útesy u Swanage patří mezi pouhá tři hlavní stanoviště orchideje pavoučí ve Velké Británii, další dvě jsou v hrabstvích Kent a Suffolk. Mluvčí Dorset Wildlife Trust uvedl: 'Jde o skvělý nález, protože orchidej pavoučí je v Británii extrémně vzácná.' Dorset i oblast Wessex Water jsou bohaté na biodiverzitu a mnoho zdejších druhů a stanovišť je zákonem chráněno. Ellen dodala: 'Je zásadní, abychom pravidelně hodnotili dopady naší činnosti na volně žijící organismy. Toto je klíčovou součástí našeho akčního plánu ochrany biodiverzity.'

article_content: Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has commended professional slackliner and balance trainer Jan Roose for capturing what he described as the 'perfect Lagos selfie.' The achievement came as Roose walked a slackline in the sky from Sterling Towers to the Onome Rig as part of a collaborative project between the Lagos State Government and energy drink brand Red Bull. In a series of tweets posted on his X (formerly Twitter) account on Saturday, Governor Sanwo-Olu celebrated Roose’s skill and creativity. He noted that Roose, a Guinness World Record-holding Estonian slackliner, successfully showcased Lagos’s vibrant spirit by blending balance training, recreation, and moving meditation during the performance. Sanwo-Olu highlighted that the selfie taken by Roose captured the beauty of Lagos’s skyline, particularly against the backdrop of the Blue Line Rail, calling it an admirable feat. He emphasized that partnering with the Lagos Safety Commission for this project further highlights the splendour of Lagos State. This event is one of several recent successful collaborations between the Lagos State Government and the Red Bull team. Other joint efforts include working with LASPARK to renovate the basketball court at Ndubuisi Kanu Park and the recent creation of Lagos Encourage Park in Ikoyi.

HÚSAVÍK, Iceland — On Tuesday, daily life in Iceland came to a halt as women across the country, joined by Prime Minister Katrín Jakobsdóttir, went on strike to demand equal pay and an end to gender-based violence. The nation witnessed schools, shops, banks, and its famous swimming pools close, while all-male news teams reported on widespread shutdowns. Public transport experienced delays, hospitals were understaffed, and hotel rooms went uncleaned as women and nonbinary individuals refused both paid and unpaid work, including household chores, in response to calls from trade unions. About 90% of Iceland’s workforce belongs to a union.

Prime Minister Jakobsdóttir announced she was joining the strike, known locally as the 'kvennaverkfall,' and expected other women in her Cabinet to follow. Despite its reputation for gender equality — Iceland has led the World Economic Forum’s gender gap ranking for 14 years — the country still experiences a gender pay gap and inequality. Tuesday’s protest echoed a historic walkout on October 24, 1975, when 90% of Icelandic women refused to work as a stand against workplace discrimination. Subsequent laws established equal gender rights, but disparities have persisted. Other partial-day strikes, most recently in 2018, have also highlighted the wage gap, symbolizing when women on average stop earning compared to men each afternoon.

Female-dominated workplaces like schools and healthcare were heavily affected by the strike. The national broadcaster RUV scaled back its programming, and only one bank branch remained open. Crowds gathered across Iceland, particularly in Reykjavik, where much of the city center was closed for rallies. Speakers addressed ongoing economic inequality and gender-based violence, challenging the notion of true equality. The audience responded with a resounding 'No!' to the question, 'You call that equality?'

Prime Minister Jakobsdóttir told mbl.is, 'We have not yet reached our goals of full gender equality and are still tackling the gender-based wage gap, which is unacceptable in 2023. Addressing gender-based violence remains a government priority.' Her Cabinet is evenly divided between men and women, and nearly half of Iceland’s legislators are women. However, lower-paid jobs like cleaning and child care are still predominantly held by women, many of whom are immigrants. Foreign women make up about 22% of the female workforce and often work longer hours for lower pay. 'Foreign women are more vulnerable,' said Alice Clarke, a Canadian artist who has lived in Iceland for 30 years. 'Hopefully today’s actions will make a difference.'

Iceland’s 1975 strike inspired similar protests worldwide, such as the 2016 women’s strike in Poland against a proposed abortion ban, and Spain’s 2018 International Women’s Day walkout. Spain’s acting equality minister Irene Montero expressed support, citing Iceland’s strike as an inspiration for Spain’s protest.

Reporting contributed by Jill Lawless in London and Ciarán Giles in Madrid for the Associated Press.

Přibližně 90 % pracovníků na Islandu je v odborech.

Premiérka Jakobsdóttir oznámila, že se ke stávce, místně zvané „kvennaverkfall,” připojí i ona, a očekávala, že ji budou následovat další ženy z její vlády. Navazující zákony zaručily rovná práva, ale rozdíly přetrvávají. Po celém Islandu, zejména v Reykjavíku, se konala shromáždění, během nichž bylo uzavřeno centrum města. Boj proti genderově podmíněnému násilí zůstává prioritou vlády.“ Její kabinet je rovnoměrně rozdělen mezi muže a ženy, téměř polovina poslanců islandského parlamentu jsou také ženy. Přesto nízko placené profese, jako je úklid a péče o děti, zůstávají převážně ženskou doménou – mnoho těchto prací vykonávají imigrantky. Islandská stávka z roku 1975 inspirovala podobné protesty i v zahraničí, například stávku žen v Polsku proti navrhovanému zákazu potratů v roce 2016 či celodenní výluku ve Španělsku na Mezinárodní den žen 8. března 2018. Španělská úřadující ministryně pro rovnost Irene Montero projevila podporu a uvedla islandskou stávku jako inspiraci španělského protestu.

article_content: France has experienced a tumultuous three weeks following footballer Nicolas Anelka's controversial goal celebration. During a match for West Bromwich Albion, Anelka dedicated his goal to comedian Dieudonné by performing the comedian’s notorious 'quenelle' gesture, which some interpret as a reverse Nazi salute. This act has sparked vigorous nationwide debate, bringing Dieudonné, a polarizing figure in French culture, into the global spotlight. Dieudonné, now 48, began his career in the 1990s as part of a comedic duo with Elie Semoun, who later found success as a film actor. Their partnership ended in 1997, after which Dieudonné began to express increasingly controversial views, drifting toward extremism and anti-Semitic rhetoric. Over the years, he has been repeatedly convicted by French courts for inciting hatred, and he has publicly supported anti-Semitic positions linked to Iran and Hezbollah. Although Dieudonné denies allegations of anti-Semitism, he claims through his lawyers that his acts are satirical, and that he is the victim of persecution for representing marginalized people in France. When venues refuse to host his shows, he routinely resorts to legal challenges. Anelka’s gesture prompted French Interior Minister Manuel Valls to investigate further, revealing an ongoing inquiry into Dieudonné for alleged money laundering and tax fraud. Valls publicly accused the comedian of attempting to declare bankruptcy to evade fines and taxes, with a possible money trail between France and Cameroon also under examination. Controversy deepened when the Interior Ministry advised regional authorities to ban Dieudonné’s shows if they posed risks to public order. This led to the banning of a performance in Nantes, which was initially overturned by an administrative court before being reinstated by the highest court in France. This legal tug-of-war is expected to recur with each of Dieudonné's scheduled performances during his tour. French President Francois Hollande expressed support for the Interior Minister’s actions. Public and media responses remain sharply divided; many French people believe that while freedom of speech is vital, it should not extend to incitement of hatred—a line they believe Dieudonné has crossed. Yet others worry that such bans may inadvertently boost his popularity, as shown by increased ticket sales. Philosopher Bernard-Henri Lévy has strongly criticized Dieudonné, arguing that his performances are no longer art but blatant political hate speech. The French government, meanwhile, faces a delicate balance between preventing hate and upholding republican values, with early indications suggesting it has made headway against racism.

Tento čin vyvolal v celé Francii vášnivou debatu a dostal Dieudonného, kontroverzní postavu francouzské kultury, do celosvětového povědomí. Dieudonné, kterému je dnes 48 let, začínal svou kariéru v 90. letech ve dvojici s Eliem Semounem, který se později prosadil jako filmový herec. Ačkoliv Dieudonné popírá obvinění z antisemitismu, jeho advokáti tvrdí, že jeho vystoupení jsou satirická a že je obětí pronásledování za to, že zastupuje vyloučené skupiny ve francouzské společnosti. Valls veřejně obvinil komika z pokusu o vyhlášení osobního bankrotu, aby se vyhnul pokutám a daním, přičemž se vyšetřuje i možný tok peněz mezi Francií a Kamerunem. Filozof Bernard-Henri Lévy Dieudonného důrazně kritizuje s tím, že jeho vystoupení už nejsou uměním, ale čistě politickou nenávistnou rétorikou. Francouzská vláda mezitím balancuje mezi potlačováním nenávisti a zachováním republikánských hodnot, přičemž první kroky naznačují úspěch v boji proti rasismu.

article_content: David Cameron has issued a strong warning that the UK is now in direct conflict with the European Union after EU leaders pushed through Jean-Claude Juncker’s appointment as President of the European Commission, ignoring British objections. Cameron labeled the process as a ‘backroom deal’ and said the move could bring the UK closer to leaving the EU. During a summit in Brussels, Cameron openly condemned Juncker’s selection, calling it a “serious mistake.” Cameron was defeated in his attempt to prevent Juncker from taking office, with the vote tally of 26 to 2 showing only Hungary alongside the UK. Despite this setback, Cameron stated he is committed to ‘winning the war’ for EU reform. Key European figures, such as EU Council President Herman Van Rompuy and German Chancellor Angela Merkel, played notable roles in the appointment; Merkel ultimately supported Juncker after initial reluctance. Juncker, the former prime minister of Luxembourg and a known supporter of deeper European integration, was nominated by the European People’s Party, the parliament’s largest group. German media ridiculed Cameron’s defeat, likening his experience to the English football team’s losses. Cameron argued that British support for the EU—which is already limited—could weaken even further because of Juncker’s presidency, particularly as the UK moves toward the planned 2017 EU membership referendum. Although Cameron criticized Juncker as a Brussels insider and a setback for EU reform, he emphasized his desire for the UK to remain within a reformed union. Cameron forecasted a prolonged effort to reclaim authority from Brussels, insisting on holding to his principles despite the unfavorable odds. He also pointed to recent European election results as a clear sign of growing dissatisfaction with how the EU operates. Although frustrated by the outcome, Cameron said he accepts the decision and will work with Juncker, but warned there will be repercussions for ignoring UK concerns. Reactions from other European leaders were mixed. Hungarian PM Viktor Orban stated his opposition to Juncker was based on principle, while Finnish PM Alexander Stubb highlighted the EU’s benefits to the UK. Labour leader Ed Miliband depicted the event as a diplomatic failure, and Eurosceptic Tory members argued that Juncker’s appointment highlights the difficulty of genuine reform within the EU. This episode has left the UK isolated in Europe and further complicated its future relationship with the European Union, especially in advance of the upcoming referendum on membership.

article_content: In a landmark moment, Pakistan’s national football team claimed their first-ever win in a World Cup qualifier, defeating Cambodia 1-0 in Islamabad. The only goal came from Harun Hamid’s half-volley, in what was Pakistan's first home match since 2015. The teams had played to a 0-0 draw in Phnom Penh beforehand. Ranked 197th worldwide, this marked Pakistan's first victory since 2018, and the win propels them into the next round, where they will contend with Saudi Arabia, Tajikistan, and Jordan starting in November. This success follows a troubled period for Pakistani football, as the team had been banned by FIFA for 15 months in 2021 due to outside interference. Pakistan now joins nine other teams in progressing from the AFC’s preliminary round, which involved two-legged ties between the continent's lowest-ranked sides. Other teams advancing include Singapore, who defeated Guam 3-1 on aggregate after a 1-0 win, and Afghanistan, which overcame Mongolia 2-0 overall. Yemen moved forward as well, securing a 4-1 win on aggregate against Sri Lanka, despite drawing 1-1 in the second leg.

Jedinou branku zápasu vstřelil Harun Hamid po půlvoleji, a šlo o první domácí utkání Pákistánu od roku 2015. Předtím týmy remizovaly 0:0 v Phnompenhu. Dicks: The Musical is a bizarre new comedy from A24 featuring outlandish elements such as sewer creatures in diapers, detached flying body parts, and outrageous family relationships. However, the film’s standout is rapper and icon Megan Thee Stallion, making her big-screen debut as Gloria Masters, the film’s assertive and charismatic boss. Clad in a power suit, Megan delivers in both song and dance in the rousing number "Out Alpha the Alpha," channeling her signature confidence and stage persona. Although Gloria only appears in two scenes and is tasked with firing the film’s self-centered twin salesmen—Craig Tiddle (Josh Sharp) and Trevor Brock (Aaron Jackson)—Megan’s presence transforms Gloria from a potential minor antagonist into one of the movie’s most memorable figures.

Gloria embodies the tough corporate manager who pushes her staff to compete, cares little for HR, and is laser-focused on profits. Despite the role’s potentially clichéd elements—unfashionable business attire and unappealing management decisions—Megan’s vibrant charisma breathes new life into every frame, making her office feel more like a lively party than a drab workplace. Gloria’s over-the-top antics, from tossing money to leading employees on leashes, are made entertaining and even subversive through Megan’s performance.

Megan Thee Stallion isn’t new to the screen, having made memorable appearances in She-Hulk: Attorney at Law and P-Valley, where she often plays larger-than-life versions of herself. She returns soon as a fun, confident character in Big Mouth and is rumored to join a Safdie Brothers Netflix project. Across all her roles, Megan embodies an unapologetically bold and feminine persona, a reflection of her music career and public image.

This consistency is far from limiting—instead, it showcases Megan’s expertise in her onstage persona and her comfort in front of the camera. As Gloria, Megan delivers an exaggerated yet authentic performance that amplifies her real-life confidence and attitude, making her a natural on screen. Her fearless approach, particularly in the face of sexist prejudice—highlighted by the 2023 conviction of Tory Lanez for the 2020 shooting—brings empowering energy to the role. Watching Megan play a powerful woman who faces challenges from men feels all the more thrilling considering her real-life experiences. In every sense, Megan Thee Stallion’s Gloria Masters is a commanding presence—making an indelible mark in her cinematic debut.
